content:
Emily Carter: Quick heads-up — opened a tiny docs PR for Dedicated capacity that touches tenant-to-pool mapping, autoscale examples, and a short note on localization of SLA language. please eyeball.
Sanjay Patel: link? :eyes:
Emily Carter: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated/1991234567-checklist (draft) — main changes are a new example mapping table and a TS SDK snippet for tenant routing.
Lauren Kim: skimmed the table, one nit: we should call out explicit behavior for tenant fallback when the reserved pool is drained.
Theo Barnes: +1 on fallback note. we also need to clarify isolation semantics — preemption vs eviction wording is confusing in current text.
Mike R.: can we add a tiny YAML autoscale example that shows min_replicas: 0 -> and explain warmup? customers trip over this.
Anna Li: I can write the wording for localization (en-GB vs en-US) for the SLA paragraph — small tech copy changes, e.g., "uptime target" vs "availability target".
Emily Carter: perfect. Sanjay can you paste the TS snippet you use in the CLI tool? I'll include as a devx example.
Sanjay Patel: sure, snippet below — keep it minimal:

```ts
// map tenant -> pool with fallback
function pickPoolForTenant(tenantId: string, mapping: Record<string,string[]>) {
  const pools = mapping[tenantId] || mapping['default'];
  // prefer first healthy pool
  return pools.find(p => isPoolHealthy(p)) || pools[0];
}
```

Sanjay Patel: note isPoolHealthy is a runtime check; mention it in the comment.
Theo Barnes: for the YAML autoscale example, propose this small fragment:

```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 0
  max_replicas: 12
  scale_cooldown: 60s
  warmup_seconds: 30
```

Theo Barnes: add a short callout below: "min_replicas: 0 allows full scale-to-zero but increases cold-start latency; use reserved_pools for low-latency tenants."
Lauren Kim: +1. Also add a short troubleshooting bullet: "If tenant sees 503s during burst, confirm fallback pools are listed and that cross-tenant isolation is not 'strict' mode."
Mike R.: about the SLA paragraph — current doc has "99.9% uptime (annual)" — suggest reword to "99.9% availability (annual, measured at infra-level)" and add a parenthetical explaining how preemption evictions affect SLA credits.
Anna Li: I'll add the alternate phrasing for localized pages: en-GB copy will use "availability" consistently; en-US can keep "uptime" with a small footnote. I'll push as a separate commit.
Emily Carter: tiny housekeeping: can someone verify internal links? I fixed one that pointed to the old terraform example.
docs-bot: link-checker ran: 3 broken links detected in branch, 2 fixed automatically, 1 remaining -> /docs/dedicated/old-terraform-snippet
Emily Carter: thanks bot. I'll remove the old snippet and replace with the new terragrunt example.
Sanjay Patel: also add a short code comment showing tenant tag priority: tenant-specific > org-default > system-default.
Anna Li: PR comment on localization: please don't pluralize "tenant" in headings for en-GB (we use singular form across product pages).
Lauren Kim: small UX ask: the mapping table should include an example "tenant tags" column to show how tags translate to pools.
Emily Carter: done in draft. last ask: can someone sanity-check the example mapping so we don't publish a policy that accidentally routes prod tenants to burst pools.
Mike R.: checked mapping, all prod tenants map to reserved-prod pool. added a CI test note: "automated guardrail prohibits mapping prod.* -> burst-*".
Theo Barnes: add that guardrail note to the migration guide section so infra folks know to run the check.
Emily Carter: awesome. I'll merge after Anna's localization commit and a +1 from Lauren on the UX table.
Lauren Kim: +1, go ahead once Anna lands wording.
Anna Li: landing in 10m.
Emily Carter: merging tomorrow morning if no regressions. thanks everyone :tada:
